title: Roghni Naan

description: Roghni Naan is a rich, soft, and slightly sweet Pakistani flatbread, traditionally baked in a tandoor. Its name comes from 'roghan', meaning oil or butter, giving it a characteristic tender texture and glossy finish. This aromatic bread is often adorned with sesame seeds and pairs wonderfully with curries, kebabs, or simply enjoyed on its own.

instructions.title: Activate the Yeast
instructions.text: In a small bowl, combine the lukewarm milk, sugar, and active dry yeast. Stir gently and let it sit for 5-10 minutes until it becomes frothy. This indicates the yeast is active.

instructions.title: Prepare the Dough
instructions.text: In a large mixing bowl, combine the sifted all-purpose flour and salt. Make a well in the center. Pour in the activated yeast mixture, beaten egg, yogurt, and 2 tablespoons of ghee or melted butter. Mix with a spoon or your hands until a shaggy dough forms.

instructions.title: Knead the Dough
instructions.text: Transfer the dough to a lightly floured surface and knead for 8-10 minutes until it becomes smooth, elastic, and no longer sticky. If the dough is too sticky, add a little more flour, one tablespoon at a time. Form the dough into a ball.

instructions.title: Proof the Dough
instructions.text: Lightly grease a clean bowl with oil. Place the dough ball in the bowl, turning it once to coat. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a damp cloth and let it rise in a warm place for 1 to 1.5 hours, or until doubled in size.

instructions.title: Shape the Naans
instructions.text: Gently punch down the risen dough and divide it into 4-6 equal portions. Roll each portion into a smooth ball. On a lightly floured surface, flatten each ball and roll it into an oval or teardrop shape, about 1/4 inch thick. Press your fingertips into the center of the naan to create indentations. Sprinkle with sesame seeds and nigella seeds, if using, and lightly press them into the dough.

instructions.title: Bake the Naans
instructions.text: Preheat your oven to its highest setting (around 250°C/480°F) with a baking stone or an inverted baking sheet inside for at least 20 minutes. Carefully transfer a shaped naan onto the hot stone/sheet. Bake for 3-5 minutes, or until puffed up and golden brown spots appear on the surface. For a more authentic look, you can finish under the broiler for 30 seconds to a minute, watching carefully to prevent burning.

instructions.title: Serve Fresh
instructions.text: Remove the baked naan from the oven and immediately brush with a little melted ghee or butter for extra shine and flavor. Repeat with the remaining dough portions. Serve hot with your favorite Pakistani curries, gravies, or kebabs.

tips: For best results, ensure your yeast is fresh and active. If it doesn't froth in step 1, your dough won't rise properly.
Don't over-flour your surface when kneading or shaping; a slightly sticky dough is better than a dry, tough one, which can lead to a hard naan.
Serve Roghni Naan immediately after baking for the softest texture and best flavor. Reheating in a hot pan or oven can revive it slightly, but fresh is always best.
